verdict.rationale: FFmpeg's official docs show format conversion (`ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi`), an explicit output bitrate option (`-b:v 64k`), and resizing through the scale filter. Encoder choice is supported by the documented H264/HEVC Vulkan encoding and by community use of h264_nvenc, and users independently call it an indispensable transcoding multitool. Missing for 10: a first-party documented codec-selection flag (e.g. -c:v) in the evidence, and an explicit resolution command example rather than only a description of the scale filter.

support.subject: As a power user, audio and video transcode between formats with control over codec, bitrate, and resolution

citations.quote: Converting video and audio has never been so easy. $ ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi
Set the video bitrate of the output file to 64 kbit/s: ffmpeg -i input.avi -b:v 64k -bufsize 64k output.mp4
followed by resizing (using the scale filter)
Support for Vulkan encoding, with H264 and HEVC was merged.
On Windows with Nvidia, h264_nvenc gives about an 8x boost
